--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.subgraph_enrichment()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Test whether a subgraph is enriched for a categorical node attribute. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.subgraph_enrichment()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Test whether a subgraph is enriched for a categorical node attribute. title: >- [Graph.subgraph_enrichment()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Test whether a subgraph is enriched for a categorical node attribute. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Test whether a subgraph is enriched for a categorical node attribute. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L47695-L47879){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.subgraph_enrichment( subgraph_nodes, attribute, target_value=None, method="hypergeometric", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Subgraph enrichment](../assets/graphs/subgraph-enrichment.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="An eight-gene network of two modules joined by the bridge G4 to G5; genes G1, G2, G3 belong to gene set X (teal) and G6, G7, G8 to set Y (violet). The tested module G1 to G4 sits in a tinted region and holds 3 of its 4 genes in set X, which has only 3 members among all 8 genes. The card gives k = 3 of n = 4, K = 3 of N = 8, fold enrichment 2.0 and hypergeometric p-value 0.071." width="100%"} Given a set of nodes (e.g., a detected community), tests whether they contain more nodes with a particular attribute value than expected by chance compared to the full graph. The test treats the graph's nodes as an urn: of `N` nodes in total, `K` carry the target value. Drawing the `n` nodes of the subgraph at random, how surprising is it to find `k` or more of them with that value? A small p-value says the subgraph is concentrated in that value beyond what chance would produce. This is the standard over-representation analysis used to interpret network modules, for example: - checking whether a detected community is enriched for a biological pathway or GO term - asking whether a cluster of customers is dominated by one region or segment - validating that a group of nodes found by some algorithm lines up with known metadata Only node membership and attribute values are used; the edges inside the subgraph play no role in the test. Nodes that lack the attribute (null values) count toward `N` and `n` but never toward `K` or `k`. To test every community from a community-detection run at once, with multiple-testing correction, use `module_annotation_enrichment()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [subgraph_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The nodes of the subgraph to test, as node IDs or string labels. Each must be in the graph, and a node listed twice counts once toward the subgraph size `n`. [attribute]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the categorical node attribute to test (e.g., `"pathway"`, `"go_term"`). Values are compared with `==`, so strings, integers, and other hashable values all work. If no node has this attribute, the result is an empty dictionary when `target_value=` is `None`, and a result with `K` and `k` of `0` otherwise. [target_value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | int | float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Specific attribute value to test enrichment for. If `None` (default), tests each distinct value separately and returns results for all. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["hypergeometric"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Statistical test to use. `"hypergeometric"` (default) computes the exact one-sided p-value `P(X >= k)` under the hypergeometric distribution, which is the appropriate test for small counts. `"chi_squared"` is a quick large-sample approximation: it computes `z = (k - E) / sqrt(E)` with `E = K * n / N` and returns the upper normal tail probability of `z`. Like the hypergeometric test it is one-sided: a subgraph with fewer hits than expected (`k < E`) gets a p-value above `0.5`, not a small one. Any other value raises a `ValueError`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `target_value=` is specified, returns a dict with keys: `"value"`, `"k"` (hits in subgraph), `"K"` (hits in graph), `"n"` (subgraph size), `"N"` (graph size), `"p_value"`, `"fold_enrichment"`. The fold enrichment is `k` divided by the expected count `K * n / N`: values above `1` mean over-representation, below `1` under-representation. If `target_value=` is `None`, returns a dict mapping each attribute value to its enrichment result dict, with values in sorted (string) order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `method=` is not `"hypergeometric"` or `"chi_squared"`, or a node in `subgraph_nodes=` isn't in the graph. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~module_annotation_enrichment`) : Test every community at once, with correction. [](`~expand_seed_set`) : Grow a module from seeds. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Six genes form two triangles, and four of the six are in the apoptosis pathway. The first triangle is all apoptosis genes, 1.5 times what chance would give, but with so few genes the p-value of `0.2` is not significant: ::: {#e8294311 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("G1", "G2"), ("G2", "G3"), ("G3", "G1"), ("G4", "G5"), ("G5", "G6"), ("G6", "G4")] ) graph.set_node_attrs( "pathway", {1: "apoptosis", 2: "apoptosis", 3: "apoptosis", 4: "signaling", 5: "signaling", 6: "apoptosis"}, ) result = graph.subgraph_enrichment(["G1", "G2", "G3"], "pathway", "apoptosis") result["fold_enrichment"], result["p_value"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1.5, 0.2) ``` ::: ::: ### What a disease module is about `proteins()` is a small protein interaction network with five known disease genes, four of them close together. `expand_seed_set()` grows those four into a module of eight proteins: ::: {#de11ea54 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} proteins = ec.proteins() module = proteins.expand_seed_set(["REP1", "REP2", "REP5", "CYC2"], min_score=0.5) proteins.plot( layout="pos", color_by="pathway", highlight=module, label_by="label" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The module holds all six DNA repair proteins in the network. Drawing 8 of the 31 proteins at random, the chance of that is about 4 in 100,000, so the module is about DNA repair.
